document.title: AmEmbassy Kabul cable 7502 to SecState, "President Amin's Desire for Better Relations"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan, 1979: Not Trump’s Terrorists, Nor Zbig’s Warm Water Ports | National Security Archive
document.note: [Confidential] Amin reached out to the Americans in early October 1979; Amstutz reports "The Afghan president made clear to me that he is open to see any designated USG mission chief." Amstutz advised against a meeting given his imminent departure on leave, a garrison mutiny against Amin, and a deplorable series of executions by the Amin regime.

events.description: Assistant Secretary Saunders testified before the Wolff Subcommittee that the initiative for better relations lay with the DRA.
Amstutz called on Foreign Minister Shah Wali, who said the initiative lay with the US.
Amstutz and Blood called on Deputy Foreign Minister Shah Mohammad Dost about the mission staff reduction; Dost replied 'Not yet'. (Cable says 'yesterday', date garbled.)
Another garrison mutiny reportedly broke out at a major military base on the outskirts of Kabul while the cable was being drafted.
The DRA reportedly executed prominent anti-communist political prisoners, including ex-Premier Etemadi, Gardak, Dr. Ali Akbar and General Shahpur.
Amstutz cabled the State Department recommending that the planned call on Amin be postponed.
Assistant Secretary Saunders testified before the Wolff Subcommittee that initiative for better relations lay with the DRA.
Amstutz informed the Deputy Planning Minister the DRA had until next spring to draw down US funds for schools and clinics (date garbled, 'OCT 6/9').
Amstutz and Blood called on Deputy Foreign Minister Dost; Dost said 'not yet' on the visa/staff reduction issue.
DRA reportedly executed Etemadi, Gardak, Dr. Ali Akbar and General Shahpur and other anti-communist prisoners; just learned of by the Embassy.
Garrison mutiny apparently broke out at a major military base (Chrishkor) on the outskirts of Kabul as cable was drafted.
Amstutz cable 7502 recommends postponing the planned call on Amin.

sources_cited: Assistant Secretary Saunders' 26 Sept 1979 statement before the Wolff Subcommittee
key_claims: Amstutz recommended postponing the call on Amin because a new garrison mutiny was reportedly under way near Kabul.
He feared the call would raise Amin's expectations of resumed US economic aid and an end to critical VOA Persian-language broadcasts.
He expected the DRA to demand continued US mission staff cuts and an end to alleged US assistance to the insurgents.
The DRA had done almost nothing on the 'visa' (mission staff reduction) problem, beyond issuing drivers' licenses to new US staff.
The DRA reportedly executed prominent anti-communist prisoners, including ex-Premier Etemadi and General Shahpur, which made a US approach to Amin seem unseemly.
Amin told Amstutz that he was open to meeting any designated US mission chief.
